clue.text: Mongrel, angry, runs into couch

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry

indicators.note: runs is set into the couch word, splitting it

parts.note: a bed is something to lie on, like a couch
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An irritable dog, wound up, charges onto the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mongrel' reads as a noun, but here it is an adjective: of mixed breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel animal has parents of different breeds, which is exactly a hybrid of mixed stock.

clue.text: Charles takes the throne, dismissing leader of traditional framework

indicators.note: the seat word drops a letter it sends away

parts.note: sits, as one does on a throne

indicators.note: the initial letter of 'traditional'

explanation.surface: King Charles is crowned, abandoning the traditional structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the throne' suggests coronation; here it simply means sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a vehicle on which the body is mounted.

clue.text: Times probing old family charity

indicators.note: the multiplication sign pokes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: fam is short for family
x is the multiplication sign, 'times'

explanation.surface: A newspaper investigates an old family's charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a well-known British aid charity working against global poverty.

clue.text: Cream stouts drunk? What an example to the boys

definitions.text: What an example to the boys

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are muddled up, as if intoxicated

explanation.surface: Drinking creamy stout would set a fine example to the lads, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is ironic: a youth leader is meant to set an example to boys, not be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scout leader is supposed to be a role model for the boys in the troop.

clue.text: Such cases will be arranged later, sir

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge's clerk tells the court the cases will be scheduled later.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrials are court cases heard a second time, so the clue's cases are of that kind.

clue.text: Harm poster, overturning iconic shot, removing head

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturning flips the poster word upside down

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a poster

indicators.note: the picture word loses its first letter

parts.note: an image is a picture, an iconic photograph

explanation.surface: A poster damages a famous photograph by cutting off its top.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage and harm are synonyms for injury or impairment.

clue.text: Energy limited by assault further down

indicators.note: energy is hemmed in, bounded on both sides, by the assault word

parts.note: a blow is a punch or attack
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fighter's strength is sapped by an attack lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something further down sits beneath, at a lower position: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Lawyers without cover missing conclusion of case

indicators.note: the uncovered word goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: bare means uncovered or naked

indicators.note: the last letter of 'case'

explanation.surface: Lawyers left exposed after missing the end of a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bar is the collective term for barristers, the legal profession.

clue.text: Forestry worker to burden a lot of people? Not entirely

parts.note: to lumber someone is to saddle them with something unwanted

indicators.note: the many word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: many means a large number of people

explanation.surface: A forester asks whether he is weighing down a crowd, only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberman fells and handles timber, a woodland job.

clue.text: Evidence of erosion around article to show impact of wind?

indicators.note: the erosion word wraps around the article

parts.note: wear is the visible sign of things being worn away
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Erosion around an object reveals the force of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone or wood exposed to the elements wears and discolours, showing the effect of wind and rain.

clue.text: Soccer organisation retreated, facing insult

indicators.note: going back means the two-letter body is written backwards

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, which runs English soccer
a front is the facing or outer face of a building

explanation.surface: Football's governing body backs down when confronted with an offensive remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate slight, a synonym for an insult.

clue.text: Successful students will retain edge in percussion instrument

indicators.note: the graduates' letters hold the edge word between them

parts.note: students who pass get degrees: MA (Master of Arts) and BA (Bachelor of Arts)
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: High achievers at college will keep their lead in the orchestra's percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a large wooden xylophone-like instrument struck with mallets, so it belongs to percussion.

clue.text: Very good month, say, to import fine item of account

parts.note: so, as in an approving 'just so', signals that all is well and right

indicators.note: the 'say' letters bring the fine word inside them

parts.note: eg (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
fine thread is thin

explanation.surface: A great month, perhaps, to bring in a top-quality item for the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item of account' is a thing of importance, as in 'that's quite something'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing of real importance, worth reckoning with, is described as being something.

clue.text: Frank, not entirely quiet, becoming cheeky

indicators.note: the frank word loses its final letter, so it is only partly there

parts.note: free speech is frank: open and unrestrained
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A man called Frank, not quite silent, starts getting impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh remark is impertinent or forward, the same as a cheeky one.

clue.text: There's a few bloggers in Beds?

definitions.text: There's a few bloggers in Beds?

parts.words: There's a few bloggers in Beds?
parts.note: a handful of web posters, read as a number plus people who post, gives the name of a canopied bed

explanation.surface: A wry aside that some online writers live in Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like Bedfordshire, an English county; it is literal beds with a post at each corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with tall posts at each corner, often with a canopy, is named for those four posts.

clue.text: After setback, golfer suppressing old expletive — or part of one?

indicators.note: a setback turns things back, so the whole assembly is read from right to left
the golfer holds the expletive down inside his name

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
bally is a dated, mild euphemism for 'bloody'

explanation.surface: A golfer, after a bad shot, stifles an old curse, or a bit of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the expletive: a single unit of a spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word divides into syllables, so each one is a piece of a word such as an oath.

clue.text: Striker having a harmful effect, ignoring leader about Nationalist

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the nationalist letter
the harm word loses its first letter

parts.note: blighting means spoiling or damaging

explanation.surface: A footballer damages the team, ignoring the captain over a nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer; it is what strikes in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt from a storm strikes the ground or a tree, so it is a striker.

clue.text: One lowering themselves socially has not left for the season

indicators.note: the person described is without the left letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: a slummer is someone who goes slumming, mixing with people of lower status

explanation.surface: A social climber in reverse stays put for the holiday period.
explanation.definitionFit: The warmest of the four parts of the year is one of the seasons.

clue.text: Pleasure to entertain learners with low light at night?

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the fun word holds the others

parts.note: fun is enjoyment
L is a learner driver; LL is plural
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Fun put on for students with dim evening lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: When the whole lunar disc is lit it gives bright light on a clear night.

clue.text: It's unfortunate about Grammar School being a complete mess

indicators.note: the regret phrase goes around the school letters

parts.note: 'it's a pity' says it is unfortunate

explanation.surface: A regretful comment on a grammar school in total chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A filthy, chaotic room is likened to a pen where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Water-bird, lake one, tucking into nut

indicators.note: the letters are tucked inside the nut word

parts.note: a pecan is a kind of nut
L is the map abbreviation for lake
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A water-bird at the lake, one of them, eating a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a pouched bill for scooping fish.

clue.text: Encounter inferior bit of beer, nothing more

parts.note: bum is slang for poor or worthless
a pint is a measure, a portion, of beer
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Meet a cheap glass of beer and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is to meet them by chance, an idiom for an unplanned encounter.

clue.text: Love English in curiously bland style associated with Wodehouse?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: curiously means the letters are put oddly together

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's prose: loving English, in an oddly bland manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' here is a style of address: Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster calls his chums this.
explanation.definitionFit: The affectionate address 'old chap' in this form is a hallmark of Wodehouse's upper-class characters.

clue.text: Material question: cracked up over that

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cracked means crazy, mad
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A query about fabric has someone going crazy over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, often silk or linen, used for tablecloths.

clue.text: Subsequent amusement concealing expression of disgust

indicators.note: the answer word hides the disgust cry inside it to make the amusement word, so take that cry out

parts.note: laughter is the sound of amusement
ugh is a cry of disgust

explanation.surface: Later fun hides a cry of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the answer, once it conceals UGH, becomes LAUGHTER, so remove UGH from LAUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something subsequent comes afterwards in time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Everyone is deceived about small item in fisherman's catch

indicators.note: the deceived word comes round to follow, sitting beside the small letter

parts.note: all means everybody
S is the clothing abbreviation for small
to be had is to be fooled or deceived

explanation.surface: Everyone is tricked over a little thing in an angler's haul.
explanation.definitionFit: The allis shad is a herring-like fish of European coasts and rivers, a possible catch for an angler.

clue.text: Surprised cry about a very strong form of Scottish beer

indicators.note: the cry goes around the other letters

parts.note: hey is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise at a very strong Scottish ale.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland beers are graded light, heavy and export; this is a darker ale like English bitter.

clue.text: Artist is chasing harmony, the strange creature

indicators.note: the artist comes after, following the harmony word

parts.note: chime means accord or harmony, as in 'chime with'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter pursues musical harmony, the odd creature.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the chimera was a fire-breathing monster combining lion, goat and serpent: a fantastical beast.

clue.text: Eradicated origin of constituency trouble

indicators.note: the parliamentary word has its opening letter wiped out

parts.note: a seat is a parliamentary constituency

explanation.surface: Losing the founding seat causes problems.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What's eating you?' means what is bothering you, so the verb means to trouble.

clue.text: Dismay complete, beginning to affect our side

parts.note: over means finished or complete

indicators.note: only the opening letter of 'affect' is taken

parts.note: we is the side that includes us

explanation.surface: Despair is total, starting to sap our team's spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to intimidate or daunt, a sense of dismay as a verb.

clue.text: Man on board heading off in the dark

indicators.note: the chess piece's name loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a knight is a chessman, a piece on the board

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a ship; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Nighttime is the dark part of the day, so 'the dark' stands for it.

clue.text: Man on board, cunning, notes English seaport

parts.note: the king is a chess piece
sly means crafty or cunning
nn is the abbreviation for notes (plural of n)

explanation.surface: A cunning chess piece gives notes on an English port.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Lynn is a port town in Norfolk on the Great Ouse estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Lynn is a historic harbour town in Norfolk on England's east coast.
